title: How to Build an IB Design Technology Study Group
summary: Build an IB Design Technology study group that stays focused from September to November with clear roles, weekly agendas, practice, and IA boundaries.
body_markdown:
An effective **IB Design Technology study group** is small, structured, and centred on evidence of learning. From September to November, meet weekly to recall content, apply concepts to products, answer exam-style questions, and set individual follow-up tasks.


The group is not a shared note-making club or an IA editing service. It should strengthen each student's independent thinking while preserving the individual authorship required for assessed work.


### Check which Design Technology course you are studying


Confirm your assessment session with your teacher before selecting topics or questions. Students taking final assessments in **2026** follow the previous course, while the revised course was first taught in 2025 for first assessment in **May 2027** .


The revised syllabus covers **Design in theory, Design in practice, and Design in context** . Paper 1 contains multiple-choice questions, Paper 2 uses short-answer and extended-response questions, and the design project remains an individual internal assessment. Older-course students have different topic numbering and, at HL, a Paper 3.


Put the course version, level, and examination session on every agenda. Check the official[IB Design Technology subject page](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/sciences/design-technology/) and[first-assessment-2027 subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/university-admission/pdfs/dp_destech_subjectbrief_en.pdf) , while following your teacher's schedule and deadlines.


### Form an accountable group


A productive group usually contains **3-5 students** . Choose members who attend reliably, prepare beforehand, and can challenge design decisions constructively.


At the first meeting, agree to:


- Meet weekly for **60-75 minutes** .
- Complete the assigned preparation.
- Keep phones away unless required for a task.
- Explain reasoning instead of supplying answers.
- Avoid sharing editable IA sections, CAD files, sketches, or evaluation text.
- Record an individual next action before leaving.


Rotate the roles of **facilitator** , **timekeeper** , **question leader** , and **recorder** . The recorder should capture misconceptions and corrections, not produce complete answers for everyone.


### Use a meeting structure that produces work


A consistent agenda keeps the session focused:


Time Activity Required output


0-10 minutes Closed-book retrieval Individual definitions, diagrams, or process steps


10-25 minutes Product application One concept applied to a real product


25-50 minutes Exam practice Individual answers followed by comparison


50-60 minutes Error review Misconceptions and corrections


60-70 minutes Planning One task and deadline per student


The **individual attempt must come before discussion** . Otherwise, confident members perform most of the thinking while others mistake recognition for understanding.


Use the[Design Technology Study Notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-design-technology-new/notes) to clarify concepts, then practise with the appropriate[Design Technology Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-design-technology/questionbank) . Revised-syllabus students can also use the[first-assessment-2027 Design Technology hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-design-technology-new) .


### Build a September-to-November plan


Strong **fall study strategies for Design Technology** move from organisation to application and integration. Match topics to your teacher's progress rather than studying unfamiliar content without context.


Period Main priority Useful group output


September Diagnose gaps and establish routines Topic audit, course check, baseline timed answers


October Apply concepts and improve explanations Product analyses, comparisons, corrected responses


November Integrate topics and review progress Mixed-topic sets, timed practice, winter priorities


In September, rate taught topics as secure, developing, or weak. Select shared weaknesses, but reserve time for individual priorities.


In October, connect concepts through products. For example, analyse how ergonomics, materials, manufacturing constraints, user needs, and circular-economy principles affect a reusable water bottle. In November, introduce mixed-topic questions, stricter timing, and an audit of repeated errors.


### Study Design Technology like designers


Practise four modes of thinking:


- **Define:** state technical vocabulary precisely.
- **Apply:** connect a concept to the product or user.
- **Analyse:** explain relationships, consequences, and trade-offs.
- **Evaluate:** reach a justified judgement using criteria or evidence.


For a material-selection task, students might separately argue for polypropylene, aluminium, or a fibre composite. Each must consider properties, manufacturing, user requirements, environmental implications, and trade-offs. Comparing arguments exposes unsupported assumptions.


Product dissection is also useful. Examine a safe everyday object, identify components and joining methods, infer manufacturing processes, and suggest measurable improvements. Reinforce vocabulary with[Design Technology Flashcards](https://www.revisiondojo.com/flashcards/ib-design-technology-new) , then use[Jojo AI](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/jojo-ai-tutor) to clarify disputed concepts after everyone attempts an explanation.


### Turn practice into measurable improvement


Do not stop when the group identifies the correct answer. Each student should annotate their own response using three labels: **knowledge** , **application** , and **reasoning** . This distinguishes a missing fact from a failure to connect that fact to the product, user, or design context.


Create an error log with the question topic, command term, cause of the error, corrected principle, and retest date. Causes should be specific, such as “confused tensile strength with toughness” or “gave advantages without weighing limitations.” Reattempt the question from a blank page one week later; rereading the model answer is not a reliable retest.


When comparing responses, ask which sentence earned credit and why. Then improve only one feature at a time, perhaps technical vocabulary, use of evidence, or the justification of a final judgement. This makes feedback actionable and prevents students from copying the strongest response without understanding it.


Once each month, complete a short closed-book mini-mock under consistent timing. Record individual marks privately, but discuss common error patterns as a group. The aim is not competition. It is to check whether weekly discussion transfers to independent performance and to decide what the next three meetings should prioritise.


### Protect individual coursework and academic integrity


The design project remains individual work. Members may discuss general concepts, practise criteria using fictional examples, or consider testing methods. They must not rewrite reports, provide ideas for direct adoption, exchange editable CAD models, or create shared wording for specifications and evaluations.


Use the protocol **question, principle, independent action** . Identify the difficulty, discuss the underlying principle, and then return independently to each project. Follow school rules and consult your teacher when uncertain. The IB[academic integrity policy](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/shared-resources/pdfs/academic-integrity-policy-en.pdf) explains the distinction between legitimate collaboration and collusion.


### Common reasons study groups fail


Vague meetings produce vague results. Replace “revise materials” with “complete five material-selection questions and rewrite one weak explanation.”


Warning signs include:


- One student teaches while everyone else listens.
- Attendance and preparation become optional.
- Members format notes instead of practising retrieval.
- Answers are discussed but never written under time pressure.
- IA progress is compared without individual action.


Review the system every three weeks. Keep activities that improve independent answers and remove those that only create activity.


### Conclusion


A successful IB Design Technology study group needs **3-5 reliable members** , a fixed weekly agenda, individual attempts before discussion, and firm academic-integrity boundaries. From September to November, progress from diagnosing gaps to applying concepts and completing mixed, timed practice.
